thread:
natalie-cs: Customer ACME (acct acme-731) escalated — their audit export for 2026-03-15 00:00-12:00 is missing ~40% of entries. They also saw elevated API latency (~400ms) during that window and client logs show `KMS decryption failed`. Escalating to infra + security. Need scope, immediate mitigation, and whether we have to notify customer now.
sarah.ops: Can you paste the customer export id or link? also want the service region.
mike_support: export id: export_20260315_acme_731_01 (from CS portal). Region: us-west-2. Customer reported failures around 08:20-08:40 PDT.
raj_infra: I'm pulling runtime traces for that timeframe. Quick check: we saw a spike in tail latency for the audit pipeline at ~08:15 with a backlog in the export worker. Also seeing repeated `504` to KMS proxy around 08:18.
elana_security: Important q: do we know if any plaintext audit log content left encrypted storage? any key rotation events on that key?
devon_eng: Not aware of KMS rotation. I can run a re-export job once we confirm reads succeed. Repro command (internal):
```
# fetch export attempts
rdwctl export fetch --id export_20260315_acme_731_01 --region us-west-2 | jq .attempts
# check kms errors
rdwctl logs query --service audit-export --since 2026-03-15T07:50:00Z --until 2026-03-15T09:00:00Z | grep KMS
```
raj_infra: Got stack traces — repeated timeouts contacting kms-proxy (upstream HSM cluster). Error shows `RPC timeout` from node-a02. Host metrics show elevated iowait on node-a02 at 08:16-08:23.
elana_security: If KMS calls failed, the files remained encrypted at rest and should not be exposed. We need to confirm whether any export attempts decrypted successfully and were delivered incomplete.
natalie-cs: Customer says the portal export shows file created but ~60% smaller than expected. They attached MD5 mismatch. They want timeline + whether data lost or delayed.
mike_support: I ran a quick compare between object sizes — exported object exists in s3 (acme-exports/2026-03-15/export_01.ndjson) but file length is ~41% smaller than expected. There are also partial upload retries in logs: `multipart upload aborted by worker` around 08:21.
raj_infra: Hypothesis: KMS timeout caused export worker to fail mid-upload and abort; the object was left truncated then replaced by a smaller completed object in a subsequent retry that omitted the failed chunk. We'll confirm by checking s3 versioning and the worker logs.
devon_eng: I'll check s3 version history now and queue a background re-export if we can successfully decrypt the source blobs. If KMS is still flaky we should avoid re-export until recovery.
elana_security: Also need to check retention policy: audit logs are retained 90 days. If the original encrypted shards are still in blobstore, we can reassemble. If any shards were purged (unlikely within 90 days) we need to escalate.
sarah.ops: @raj_infra can you capture the following for the incident ticket: list of affected files, worker ids, KMS key alias (alias/rdw/audit/acme-731), and whether HSM reported any maintenance window?
raj_infra: Captured: affected files: acme-exports/2026-03-15/*; worker ids: audit-worker-07, audit-worker-11; kms alias: alias/rdw/audit/acme-731; HSM control plane shows a transient degraded period 08:16-08:24 with increased RPC latency — no scheduled maintenance.
incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-03-15-87 (severity: P2). Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-03-15-87
mike_support: Proposed immediate next steps: 1) freeze new exports for acme-731 (prevent more partials) 2) check s3 versions for full object 3) attempt decrypt of source shards with a small test job 4) if decrypt ok, run re-export and validate MD5 before handing back to customer.
elana_security: Agree. Also prepare a short customer notification: explain incident, confirm no plaintext exfiltration, and give ETA for re-export. Keep wording non-technical.
natalie-cs: CS draft for customer (we will edit): "We identified an issue during your audit export on 2026-03-15 that resulted in an incomplete file. Our engineers are investigating; the issue was caused by transient key-management timeouts which prevented some chunks from being finalized. We do not believe any unencrypted data was exposed. We will provide an ETA for a corrected export within 6 hours." Thoughts?\elana_security: Clean enough. Add: we will confirm whether any replays are possible and offer to provide the full export as soon as verified.
devon_eng: Update: I could decrypt a sample shard locally using `kms-decrypt --key alias/rdw/audit/acme-731 --input shard_12345.enc` and it succeeded (fast). So KMS seems responsive from staging. Production issues look tied to node-a02 RPC timeouts.
raj_infra: Actions done: restored node-a02 network path to KMS proxy (bumped conn pool), restarted audit-worker-07. We'll monitor for retries.
mike_support: If re-export succeeds, recommend we run customer validation on a signed checksum and optionally give them the older version if s3 versions show a prior complete object.
sarah.ops: Timeline check — can we commit to ETA 6 hours? current time is 10:12 PDT. That would be ~16:12 UTC. Ops/SRE, confirm.
raj_infra: With decrypt verified and node fix in place, a targeted re-export should finish within 2-3 hours. I'll mark ETA 3 hours to be safe.
natalie-cs: Okay — I'll send customer a first notification now with conservative ETA 6 hours and promise a more concrete update in 2 hours.
elana_security: Also add to the incident record that this is likely an operational HSM/client RPC latency issue, not key compromise. We'll do a postmortem and check HSM audit logs.
natalie-cs: I'll draft the customer message and post it to #incident-communications for review before sending. Thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:"
